page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with two threads per physical core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2. The instance includes 120 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled, requiring network-attached persistent disks for storage, and it includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results show a distinct division between single-threaded throughput and parallelized multi-core performance. Single-core evaluations reflect legacy architecture limitations, with Geekbench single-core scoring 922.0 and stress-ng single-core scoring 1115.89, both ranking in the lower performance brackets. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (19.52 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.17 GB/sec) also perform in the bottom 10%. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reach mainstream median thresholds, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 23,520.43, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,982.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 20,859.21.

Memory and application metrics similarly place the instance in mid-tier throughput ranges. Uncached read bandwidth reaches 101.81 GB/sec with write bandwidth at 46.41 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 1,305.99 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks highlight balanced concurrency, recording 21.91 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 18.23 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference yields moderate throughput on small to medium models, processing 41.73 prompt tokens per second and 12.11 generation tokens per second on a 7B model, though scaling falls sharply on 70B models.

The hardware configuration provides high core counts and substantial memory density for parallel workloads, though its individual core efficiency is lower than modern architectures. Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, compiling software, distributed caching nodes, static web serving clusters, and enterprise application hosting that do not demand cutting-edge single-thread latency.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.3 GHz and 120 GB of memory (3.75 GB per vCPU). Based on the x86_64 architecture with a 45 MB L3 cache, the system does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal modest single-thread capabilities, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 922.0 and lower-tier compression throughput. However, its multi-core scaling reaches median industry levels, delivering 23,520.43 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 20,859.21. Memory bandwidth achieves 101.81 GB/sec for large uncached reads, supporting strong concurrent throughput like 21.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.23 GB/sec in static web serving. This instance fits multi-threaded general-purpose compute, build pipelines, enterprise backends, and caching tiers.
